sources.beginner: Prompt names the Suite Decision Tree Builder (src/pages/apps/DecisionTreeBuilder.jsx): KPI cards fmtMM maximumFractionDigits 2 (:26), tree diagram node labels 0/1/2 decimals by magnitude (src/components/decisiontree/TreeDiagram.jsx:17-21); every value is also a hand rollback taught in beginner m04 and m06/l02. NextGen TreeExplorer is EKPAN/OKRIKA only (panelCapstoneGuard.test.js).
sources.intermediate: No app named for fields 1-5: Bayes and value-of-information hand-calcs taught in intermediate m01-m04 and m06/l02 (full precision). Field 6 is the two-action value the VOI Analyzer would compute (engine voi.js returns two-decimal strings, ResultsPanel.jsx:62), also a hand-calc from m05.
sources.advanced: Three-reading Bayes and the consistency boundary are hand-calcs (advanced m01, m02, m06/l02); the MC-linked root EMV reads from the Decision Tree Builder (fmtMM 2 decimals) or by hand; the decision advantage row comes from Decision Studio's brief (src/components/decisionstudio/briefModel.js:87-89, fmtMM toFixed(1)); the Analyzer EVPI card is a two-decimal string (packages/engines/engines/economics/voi.js:217).

fields.prompt_precision: Money to four decimals in million USD

fix.display: src/pages/apps/DecisionTreeBuilder.jsx:26 -> fmtMM prints minimumFractionDigits 4, maximumFractionDigits 4 (KPI cards: Optimal EMV, Next best alternative, Decision advantage); src/components/decisiontree/TreeDiagram.jsx:17-21 -> node and branch labels print 4 decimals (or add a selected-node readout at 4 decimals if the diagram gets too busy)

fields.recommendation: Display fix. The prompt names the Decision Tree Builder and asks for four decimals, but its KPI cards print at most 2 decimals (toLocaleString maximumFractionDigits 2) and the diagram prints 0 decimals at or above 100 and 1 decimal from 10 to 100. The rollback is also a hand-calc taught in beginner m04 and m06/l02, which passes at full precision, so no learner is locked out today; a learner who reads the app is. Widening tol cannot rescue the 0-decimal node labels without making the field meaningless.
fields.evidence: Diagram node label `EMV ${fmt(emv)}` uses 0 decimals at or above 100, printing 469 against 469.386 (tol 0.001). Hand rollback 0.62 x 684.2 + 0.38 x 118.9 = 469.386 exactly.

fields.prompt_precision: the indicator chance in percent to four decimals
fields.evidence: Implied prior per outcome is s x Strong_k + (1-s) x Weak_k; the largest s keeping every delta within 0.005 of the stated prior solves a linear inequality, 39.058824; four decimals (39.0588) is within tol 0.001.
fields.notes: The Analyzer only reports consistent true/false at a typed value, so bisection in the app is possible but the linear solve is the taught route.
